title: Cinderella
place: A household and royal festival in old Germany
sourceAuthor: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm; translated by Marion Edwardes
note: A new adaptation of the Grimms’ “Cinderella,” retaining the hazel tree and birds rather than details from later screen adaptations. Violent punishments are omitted.

rights.basis: The 1912 English source edition is identified as public domain in the United States by Project Gutenberg.

artLabel: Cinderella stands beneath a hazel tree as white birds bring a silver dress and golden slipper.

pageArt.alt: White birds bring Cinderella a shining dress and golden slippers beneath the hazel tree.
A royal messenger discovers that the golden slipper fits Cinderella.

scenes: After her mother died, a girl was made to work among the ashes by her stepsisters, who mockingly called her Cinderella.
She planted a hazel twig at her mother’s grave and watered it with her tears until it grew into a tree.
When the king announced a three-day festival, the stepsisters scattered lentils into the ashes to keep Cinderella home.
White birds came to help her sort every grain.
At the hazel tree, Cinderella asked for something fine to wear. The birds brought a shining dress and slippers, and she went to the festival, where no one recognized her.
Each night she slipped away before her family returned. On the third night, one golden slipper remained behind on the palace stair.
The royal messenger searched until the slipper fit Cinderella. Her fine clothes had not made her worthy; they had only allowed others to see the person the ashes had hidden.
She left the old household and began a life in which kindness was no longer treated as weakness.
